newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices stay buoyant underpinned by winter demand.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices stay buoyant underpinned by winter demand.

text.p: World oil prices shaved some of their recent sharp gains on Wednesday but remained underpinned by concerns over the supply of heating oil to Western markets approaching winter.
London November futures for bellwether Brent crude were down 11 cents a barrel at $22.85 a barrel at 1658 GMT, after jumping 70 cents on Tuesday, but remain $5 above levels at this time last year.

European heating oil prices on Wednesday morning hit five-year highs after the latest weekly U.S. inventory data released late on Tuesday showed heating oil stocks in the world's biggest market still well below normal.
October London heating oil futures hit $228 a tonne for the first time since August 1991.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) said distillates stocks, comprising heating oil and diesel, rose just 300,000 barrels to 112 million and still 19 million below year-ago levels.
"The API numbers were yet again supportive for heating oil," said energy analyst Charles Gray at futures brokers Prudential Bache.
"The distillate build was well below expectations," said brokers GNI. "The weather in Europe has turned colder, which is sparking further concern in the heating oil market."
Traders on Wednesday played down the significance for oil prices of Boris Yeltsin's health problems after concerns about the Russian president helped lift markets on Tuesday.
Yeltsin on Wednesday was given the go-ahead for heart surgery and doctors said they were confident the operation would be successful.
Analysts said a change in the Russian presidency was unlikely to have much impact on oil exports from the country which relies heavily on crude and product revenues for hard currency earnings.
"Oil revenue is extremely important to the cash-strapped economy, so any new leader is unlikely to tinker too much with the industry," said brokers GNI.
